title: Jurisdictional handback procedures and test cases
content:
Context:
This doc captures an operational pattern were calling 'handback' — the controlled movement of a tenants request routing and data-handling authority from global-hosted paths into a jurisdictional boundary (customerpin / sovereign anchor) and back when necessary. It complements region-pin enforcement by explicitly documenting the evidence, telemetry and test cases needed to declare a successful handback to legal / audit teams.

Goal:
- Provide operators and engineers with a repeatable runbook for initiating a handback, validating evidence, running end-to-end tests, and rolling back if evidence fails.
- Define test cases (automated + manual) to prove residency for audit windows.
- Surface integration contract changes required in API and routing layers for safe handback transitions.

Assumptions:
- Customer has an active 'sovereign anchor' (regional cluster or VPC) and a pin configured in tenant metadata.
- Handback is initiated when routing policy needs to move a active tenant session off global infra (e.g., legal escalation, incident containment, customer request).
- We have pre-approved legal criteria for evidence (access logs, commit hashes, network topology snapshot).

Quick operator checklist (pre-handback):
1) Verify tenant pin: GET /internal/tenant/{tenant_id}/pin -> tenant_pin present and matches region code.
2) Confirm capacity reservation in target anchor: console /dedicated/anchors/{anchor_id}/capacity -> green.
3) Collect pre-handback snapshot: 
   - orchestration commit id (k8s/helm)
   - routing table dump (time-stamped)
   - KV-cache snapshot id (if applicable)
4) Notify SRE-on-call and Legal via #residency with JIRA ticket ENG-4321 linked.

Handback execution (operator):
- Step A: Quiesce new session routes to anchor. Set soft-fail window = 30s to let in-flight prefetched keys finish.
- Step B: Switch routing policy: PATCH /routing/policy/{tenant_id} body {"mode":"anchor-handback","target":"eu-west-1-anchor-22","reason":"legal-escrow"} (sample payload below).
- Step C: Verify envoy/proxy connectivity to anchor + circuit health (3 successful health checks).
- Step D: Record post-switch evidence bundle: logs, routing table, network topology, KMS key location. Attach to JIRA.

Sample API payload (internal only):
{
  "mode":"anchor-handback",
  "target":"eu-west-1-anchor-22",
  "grace_seconds":30,
  "evidence_batch_id":"evid-20250214-pt1",
  "initiated_by":"priya.patel@redwood.com",
  "reason":"regulatory-escrow"
}

Validation gates (automated):
- Gate 1: Routing assertion: telemetry shows >=95% of new requests for tenant_id routed to target anchor for 5m window. (metric: routing.percent_to_target).
- Gate 2: Storage residency: object-store path prefixes for tenant_data point to anchor-backed bucket and KMS key id matches approved anchor KMS (metric: storage.kms_match=true).
- Gate 3: Latency SLOs: p95 for anchor-bound requests within expected SLA (p95_anchor <= baseline_p95*1.5). Failure triggers rollback.

Evidence package (minimum):
- routing-table-{timestamp}.json (signed by routing-service)
- anchor-deploy-commit.txt (git sha + image digest)
- access-logs.zip (first 15 minutes post-switch)
- kms-key-manifest.txt
- network-snapshot.pcap (only if requested by Legal)

Test cases (matrix):
1) Basic routing test (automated): create test session for tenant, assert route header X-Anchor == eu-west-1-anchor-22, assert 200 OK.
2) Failover test (chaos): simulate anchor node flapping, ensure fallback policy routes to fallback-anchor with documented SLA hit.
3) Evidence integrity test (manual + script): sign/verify evidence bundle with platform signing key.
4) Cross-border leak test: send synthetic request with IP from disallowed country and assert request rejected or routed to quarantine.
5) Short-lived session rollover: open long-polling session, initiate handback mid-session, validate KV-cache migration or TTL-coherence.

Integration changes to be landed in next sprint:
- routing service: add explicit "handback_reason" field in audit logs (ENG-4321).
- telemetry: new metric routing.handback_success_rate with labels {tenant, anchor, operator} (PR: #289).
- SDKs: add client-side hint header X-Region-Preference for customers optionally controlling soft-pin behaviour.

Rollback / remediation steps:
- Immediate rollback: PATCH routing/policy -> {"mode":"global","reason":"handback-failed-rollback"}.
- Evidence reconciliation: compare pre/post snapshots, mark mismatch fields and escalate to SRE+Legal.
- Customer comms: use template 'handback-failure-notice-v1' from Confluence.

Operator runbook notes (practical tips):
- When collecting evidence, always timestamp files with UTC and include the operator username.
- If KMS mismatch occurs, do not proceed to finalize the handback. Escalate to Security.
- For high-throughput tenants, enable traffic-sampling to keep evidence size manageable (1% sample + deterministic keys).

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Q1: What is the minimal retention window for evidence per legal? (Legal: Marco to confirm whether 90 days OK.)
- Q2: How do we sign evidence bundles in air-gapped customer anchors? (Proposal: use ephemeral signing token exchanged via out-of-band.)
- Q3: Can we automate anchor capacity reservation during handback to avoid operator step? (Follow-up: design spike in sprint 23.)

Next steps / action items:
- [Priya] Draft API spec change and post to eng-architecture for review (due 2025-02-21).
- [Liam] Wire up telemetry metric and add unit tests (PR #289).
- [Sofia] Run tabletop with Legal and SRE on 2025-02-25 and record minutes.
- [Jonas] Add automated test coverage in staging for 'short-lived session rollover' case.

Notes to self: keep language provisional until Legal confirms evidence format. This doc is intended as operator-facing, not customer-facing. Archive final evidence bundle in /evidence-buckets/tenant-handbacks/ only after Legal signs off.

Attachments (reference checklist):
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/internal/RESID-508 (design + legal template)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4321 (handback feature epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/region-routing/pull/289

End of doc.
